sections.title: Ratios
sections.text: A ratio compares two quantities that use the same units. The ratio of a to b is written a/b, a to b, or a:b. Ratios are usually simplified the same way fractions are, by dividing both parts by their greatest common factor.

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: A rate compares two quantities with different units, like miles per hour. A unit rate has a denominator of 1, found by dividing the numerator by the denominator. Example: driving 300 miles in 5 hours is a rate of 300 miles / 5 hours, which simplifies to a unit rate of 60 miles per hour.

sections.title: Solve Proportions
sections.text: A proportion is an equation stating that two ratios (or rates) are equal, written a/b = c/d. To solve a proportion for an unknown, cross-multiply: a*d = b*c, then solve the resulting equation. Example: x/4 = 15/20. Cross-multiply: 20x = 60, so x = 3.
